task.title: Escaped defects are invisible — we cannot tell whether the gauntlet works
task.body:
## What is wrong

Upheld sampled-audit disagreements land in `escape_ledger.jsonl` and nowhere
else. Reading them today means SSHing to the host and `jq`-ing a JSONL file, so
nobody reads them. The escape rate that `SampledAuditLoop` exists to measure is
invisible to the people deciding whether the gauntlet is working.

## Why it matters now

There are three open proposals to add gates (spec-match strictness, a second
ultra-review pass, and a plan-compliance ratchet) and no way to tell whether the
two gates we added in June changed anything. Every one of those arguments is
currently settled by whoever is most confident in the room.

## What we know

- `escape_ledger.jsonl` on the 2026-07-19 host has 41 rows.
- 17 of them carry `detection_source: sampled-audit`; the rest are
  customer-reported or found by a later diagnostic run.
- `EscapeLedger.read_all()` already streams rows and carries the blast-radius
  stratum per record (`src/escape/ledger.py:88`).
- The Insights tab already has a gate-health panel and a review-insight pattern
  panel, so there is a place to put something.

## Constraints

- Read-only. The audit loop is a sensor and must stay one (ADR-0029).
- Whatever we build must not require a schema migration on the ledger.
- The dashboard is server-rendered partials plus a small amount of JS; no new
  front-end framework.

## Explicitly not asking for

- Changing the sampling rate or the governor.
- Emailing or Slacking anything.

args.stall_context:
The implement phase ran twice on #9812 and both attempts ended at the quality
gate rather than at a review. Preflight escalated after attempt 2.

**Attempt 1** (branch `hydraflow/9812-escape-digest`, 4 files, +96/-9)
- `make quality` failed: 1 failing test, 1 ruff finding.
- `tests/test_escape_digest.py::test_build_digest_handles_year_boundary` — a
  record dated 2024-12-30 buckets as `2025-W01` (correct per ISO 8601) but the
  test asserts `2024-W52`, and the agent could not decide which side was wrong.
  It flipped the assertion, then flipped it back, then rewrote the helper to
  special-case December, which broke
  `test_build_digest_orders_weeks_newest_first`.
- `ruff F401` on `src/server_routes_insights.py`: `Query` imported for the
  window validation but the validation itself was never added.

**Attempt 2** (same branch, +11 more lines)
- Reverted the December special-case, restored the ISO behaviour, and
  `test_build_digest_orders_weeks_newest_first` went green again.
- `test_build_digest_handles_year_boundary` still fails — the agent left the
  test asserting `2024-W52` and wrote a comment saying "confirm intent with a
  human" instead of resolving it.
- `ruff F401` persists.
- The agent then began the `SampledAuditLoop` change (writing `merged_at` into
  `detected_at` instead of `audited_at`) and the Insights partial in the same
  attempt, and ran out of turns with the loop change half-applied.

**Work already on the branch (diff-so-far, summarised)**
- `src/escape/digest.py` — NEW, 58 lines. `WeekBucket` plus `build_digest`. Its
  two grouping tests (`..._groups_two_records_in_one_week`,
  `..._orders_weeks_newest_first`) passed at the end of BOTH attempts. This part
  of the branch is sound and reviewable on its own.
- `src/server_routes_insights.py` — `GET /api/insights/escape-digest` added,
  takes `weeks: int = 8` with no bounds, returns a bare bucket list. Carries the
  unused `Query` import that is failing ruff.
- `src/sampled_audit_loop.py` — `_record_upheld` half-edited: it now writes
  `sample.merged_at` but still passes `detection_source` only, so the
  blast-radius stratum the shaped direction asked for is not carried, and a
  `self._digest_cache.invalidate()` call was added referencing an attribute that
  is never constructed.
- `src/static/js/insights.js` — untouched. The UI was never started.
- `tests/test_escape_digest.py` — 3 tests, 2 green, 1 red.

**Observed pattern across both attempts:** the agent kept context-switching
between the pure aggregation, a semantics decision about a persisted field, and
transport/UI wiring, and never finished any of the three.
args.doc_context:
## ADR-0029 — Caretaker loop pattern (Accepted)

Caretaker loops are read-only sensors. A caretaker never edits code, opens a fix
PR, or gates a merge. Its output is an append-only record other components may
read. **Consequence relevant here:** any change inside a caretaker tick body
that can raise will stop that tick from recording, and a caretaker that stops
recording fails silently — there is no consumer to notice.

## ADR-0021 — Persistence architecture and data layout (Accepted)

Append-only JSONL under the repo-scoped data root. Rows are never rewritten in
place. **Consequence relevant here:** there is no migration mechanism for
existing rows. Changing the meaning of a field on new rows leaves old rows
carrying the old meaning forever, so a reader must either tolerate both or the
cut-over must be recorded.

## ADR-0115 — Sampled-audit adjudication (Accepted)

`SampledAuditLoop` re-audits a governed sample of merged PRs with fresh context
and no sight of the original gauntlet verdicts. Upheld disagreements are
cross-linked into the escape ledger with `detection_source: sampled-audit`. The
disagreement rate is an independent bound on escaped defects. **Consequence
relevant here:** the loop is the factory's only independent quality sensor, so
its blast radius is higher than its line count suggests.

## Wiki — `docs/wiki/architecture-layers.md`, "Pure aggregation modules"

Aggregation helpers under `src/<area>/` stay pure: no I/O, no config
construction, no framework imports. The route layer owns reading and validation.
Mixing them is the single most common cause of an aggregation helper that cannot
be unit-tested.

## Wiki — `docs/wiki/patterns.md`, "Dashboard empty states"

Every dashboard panel distinguishes three states: a real zero, no data at all,
and a failed fetch. An empty table that could be any of the three has twice been
mistaken for an outage (#9540, #9702).
